items.title: آنچه گذشت؛ دو ایتالیایی در حمله پهپادی به تاسیسات نظامی کویت کشته شدند
items.summary: در پی کشته شدن دو ایتالیایی در حمله پهپادی به کویت، ایران هرگونه نقش در این حمله را تکذیب کرد. دولت ایتالیا می‌گوید این دو نفر روی پدافند هوایی کار می کردند و در «حمله پهپادی ایران» به مرکز رادار تاسیسات نظامی کویت کشته شدند. کویت هم این حمله را به ایران نسبت داده است. اما هم سخنگوی ارشد نیروهای مسلح ایران و هم سفارت جمهوری اسلامی در رم، هرگونه نقش تهران در این حمله را رد کرده‌اند. رئیس کمیسیون اروپا در واکنش به این حمله خواستار افزایش فشار بر ایران شد.

items.title_original: How to spot real Black Friday savings this holiday season amid the affordability squeeze
items.summary: معاملات جمعه سیاه همه جا وجود دارد، اما قیمت فروش همیشه به معنای پس انداز واقعی نیست. در شرایطی که بودجه‌ها تحت فشار هستند، در بحبوحه تداوم بحران مقرون‌به‌صرفه و افزایش قیمت سوخت با درگیری شدید ایران، خریداران به دنبال راه‌هایی برای افزایش پول خود در فصل خرید تعطیلات امسال هستند. پیش بینی ها حاکی از فصلی از هزینه های محتاطانه است. Visa Business and Economics Insights انتظار دارد فروش تعطیلات 4.5 درصد نسبت به سال گذشته افزایش یابد – اما پس از محاسبه قیمت‌های بالاتر، افزایش واقعی خرید خریداران تنها 1.1 درصد پیش‌بینی می‌شود. این موضوع اهمیت بیشتری برای خریداران می‌دهد که بدانند برای چه چیزی پول می‌پردازند و آیا فروش واقعاً یک معامله است. دینش گاوری، یک مارک، "هنوز زمان خوبی برای خرید است. فقط باید کمی مراقب باشید."
items.summary_original: Black Friday deals are everywhere, but a sale price does not always mean real savings. With budgets under pressure, amid a persisting affordability crisis and rising fuel prices with the raging Iran conflict, shoppers are looking for ways to stretch their money during the holiday shopping season this year. The forecasts point to a season of cautious spending. Visa Business and Economics Insights expects holiday sales to increase 4.5% from last year — but after accounting for higher prices, the actual increase in what shoppers buy is projected to be just 1.1%. That makes it all the more important for shoppers to know what they’re paying for and whether a sale is truly a deal. "It's still a good time to shop. It's just that you just have to be a little bit more careful," Dinesh Gauri, a marketing professor at the University at Buffalo, told Fox News Digital when discussing holiday and Black Friday shopping. 7 HOLIDAY SHOPPING SCAMS TO WATCH FOR THIS SEASON Gauri revealed that shopping during Black Friday does not always produce the best deal — especially when it comes to essential technology like cell phones. He advised shoppers to set a budget and research prices before making a purchase, especially for big-ticket items. "Have a number in mind and do your research before you go about spending the money," he said, recommending price-tracking sites and extra promotions. items.summary_original: Strobe Talbott, a former deputy secretary of state whose deep expertise on the Soviet Union shaped U.S. foreign policy before he went on to lead the Brookings Institution, died Thursday at the age of 80. Talbott’s son, Devin Talbott, said his father died peacefully after a long illness at his home in East Hampton, New York, The Associated Press reported. An Ohio native, Talbott began his journalism career as an intern at Time magazine while studying at Yale and Oxford, where he was roommates with future President Bill Clinton . Clinton later joked that his job in their shared apartment was to make Talbott breakfast every morning. NATO WARNS PUTIN COULD STRIKE BEFORE EUROPEAN ARMY RESPONDS, POINTS TO US AS MILITARY MODEL While at Time, Talbott was tapped to translate the leaked memoirs of Nikita Khrushchev, the former Soviet leader ousted in 1964, which earned him a full-time role at the magazine. Over a 21-year career there, he focused on U.S.-Soviet relations, led the Washington bureau, and wrote as a foreign affairs columnist. In 1994, Talbott joined the Clinton administration as deputy secretary of state, helping guide U.S. relations with Russia and other post-Soviet states. In a statement, Bill Clinton said no one was better suited to advise him on Russian affairs than Talbott, noting that former Secretary of State Hillary Clinton also relied on his counsel. items.summary_original: Russian President Vladimir Putin's control over Crimea faced renewed pressure Thursday as a massive blackout crippled the Russian-occupied peninsula, disrupting public transport and leaving people without heat, according to reports. The blackout came after Ukrainian strikes had damaged the Kerch Strait Bridge last week, disrupting a key Russian military supply route, and as Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy warned that Moscow was preparing another large-scale attack on Ukraine. Russian-controlled utilities blamed the Crimea blackout on an accident at energy facilities outside the region, after reports of explosions and air raid sirens sounded across the Black Sea peninsula, according to the Kyiv Post . items.summary_original: Under a cloak of secrecy, two American presidents made surprise Thanksgiving visits to war zones, bringing a taste of home to U.S. troops serving thousands of miles from their families. Sixteen years apart, President George W. Bush celebrated with American troops in Iraq in 2003, while President Donald Trump served Thanksgiving dinner to service members in Afghanistan in 2019. Both visits were carried out under tight secrecy, catching troops by surprise as they spent the holiday far from home. Trump secretly traveled to Bagram Airfield in Afghanistan on Nov. 28, 2019, when he served turkey, posed for photos and thanked American troops for their sacrifices amid the ongoing war. INSIDE TRUMP’S INTIMATE MEETING WITH NATION’S BRAVEST SOLDIERS DURING WHIRLWIND TEXAS TRIP "There's nowhere I'd rather celebrate this Thanksgiving than right here with the toughest, strongest, best and bravest warriors on the face of the Earth," Trump told the troops at the time, later adding, "And you don't even know how much the people of our country love and respect you." The visit came as roughly 12,000 American troops remained in Afghanistan more than 18 years after the U.S. invasion. "I'm thankful for family ," Rep. Eric Burlison, R-Mo., told Fox News Digital. "It's what drives me to keep going, to keep doing this, keep fighting for the country." Families across America are gathering for Thanksgiving, kicking off a holiday season that's meant for reflection and refocusing on things that matter most. And members of Congress who spoke with Fox News Digital about that special day are no different. "You know, elections can be a bumpy road in many ways, and it's easy to take a shot at somebody who's running — we put ourselves out there. items.summary_original: A former adviser to Iran's nuclear negotiating team accused Ukraine on Thursday of orchestrating a deadly drone attack in Kuwait to prove its worth to President Donald Trump, as Tehran continued to deny responsibility. And while Kuwaiti and Italian officials blamed Iran for the strike, which killed two Italian defense technicians and wounded two others, Iran’s embassy in Rome warned against "false flag" operations it said were aimed at widening the Persian Gulf conflict and now drawing Europe into the crisis. Mohammad Marandi, who served as an adviser during talks with the U.S. in Pakistan and has been dubbed Iran's " English-language mouthpiece ," claimed Ukrainian forces were operating across the Middle East, including in northern Iraq and Syria, also in remarks reported by the Fars News Agency, which is affiliated with the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC). items.summary_original: Thanksgiving is a day of celebration and spending time with family for the vast majority of Americans, but for several students on college campuses across the country, the national holiday is a source of anguish that is being expressed in the form of protests and counter-programming events. On Nov. 18, George Washington University hosted an event called "Breaking Bread: The Cost of Celebration" that was described as a chance for students to examine Thanksgiving, Christmas and Independence Day through an intersectional lens, including experiences of "belonging, exclusion, cultural erasure, and historical harm." "Through facilitated dialogue and shared reflection, students will engage in meaningful conversations about historical memory, social responsibility, and the complexities of celebrating within a diverse society," the student life event description read. At the University of Wisconsin at Milwaukee, the American Indian Student Center Electa Quinney Institute for American Indian Education hosted a Nov. 17 event called "AlterNative Giving," which was described as "a community gathering that offers a meaningful alternative to the traditional Thanksgiving narrative. Instead of focusing on colonial histories, we come together to honor Indigenous ways of knowing, being, and giving." Britain's Ministry of Defence has written to former service members to verify their contact information and military skills to ensure the country is prepared for a national emergency or potential conflict, Secretary of State for Defence Wes Streeting confirmed Friday. The outreach comes as the International Institute for Strategic Studies warned Thursday that suspected Russian-directed sabotage across Europe could trigger a "mass-casualty event." Researchers warned that a major attack could spark calls for retaliation and divide European governments. "I want the country to be alert, not alarmed," Streeting told BBC Radio 4's "Today" program. "You can't not look at what's going on in Europe and not be concerned about a threat environment which has deteriorated in recent years and is sadly increasing," he said. The holiday post mixed praise for "AMERICAN PATRIOTS" with criticism of the "Radical Far Left" and Minnesota’s Somali community, which Trump has frequently accused of public assistance fraud in the state. "I want to thank the 2% of our Somalian population that have a job, and are actually willing to work, without receiving Government Assistance," Trump wrote in the post. "These are wonderful American ‘citizens,’ and should be allowed to stay in our Country, and celebrate Thanksgiving with us. The others should be thrown out, immediately, thereby saving the Great State of Minnesota, which has no chance if they are allowed to stay." items.summary_original: North Korea has temporarily halted shipments of ballistic missiles and artillery shells to Russia following diplomatic friction between the two allies over Moscow's outreach to South Korea, Ukrainian military intelligence said Thursday. According to Ukraine's GUR military intelligence agency, North Korean Foreign Minister Choe Son Hui announced the freeze on KN-23 ballistic missile and artillery deliveries last month after Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Andrey Rudenko suggested Moscow would help de-escalate tensions between Seoul and Pyongyang, Reuters reported. Choe demanded that Russia clarify its policy toward South Korea, GUR said, though Reuters noted it could not independently verify the report or confirm public remarks from either official. PUTIN'S WAR DEATH TOLL REPORTEDLY TOPS 700,000 AS RUSSIA SCRAMBLES FOR RECRUITS The reported pause also suspends Russian military flights over North Korea and stalls a Kremlin request to expand North Korea's troop deployment in Russia from roughly 8,500 to 50,000, according to the outlet. Rudenko, who oversees Asian relations, said last month that Seoul had signaled interest in normalizing ties and resuming direct flights with Moscow once the Ukraine war ends. Despite the reported freeze, North Korean troops remain active in Russia, with 11th Corps units serving in the Kursk region and a missile unit operating in Voronezh since mid-summer, GUR said. items.summary_original: As Americans across the country sit down to Thanksgiving dinner just weeks after Democrats' midterm sweep drastically reshaped the political landscape going into 2027, conversations about politics and the economy could turn tense. Dr. Joel Davis Brown, a leadership expert, executive coach and author who studies how people communicate and navigate conflict, says swapping out the word "but" when discussing controversial topics can help keep the discussions civil. "‘But’ shows disagreement," Brown told Fox News Digital. "It’s a way of telling the person that what they said should not be heard, and it really stifles conversation." Instead, Brown suggests trying "yes, and." That doesn’t mean you have to agree, he said. Rather, it signals that you’ve heard the other person and leaves room to share a different view. "‘Yes, I’ve heard you and I have a different opinion,’" Brown said. "We can listen to varying opinions." FOOD PRICES ARE RISING BEFORE THANKSGIVING. AN ECONOMIST SHARES WAYS TO SAVE If a hot-button topic comes up, Brown recommends asking the person to "tell me more about that." The question, he says, can help you understand how someone arrived at their view instead of turning the exchange into a debate. He also cautions against opening with "I disagree," which can put people "in an oppositional place" before they have fully heard one another. items.summary_original: FlyDubai announced Thursday it will resume flights to Tel Aviv, Israel, next week, ending a suspension in place following an attempted hijacking incident in late September, according to media reports. A source familiar with the matter told The Times of Israel that the airline is being allowed back into Israeli airspace "under new security arrangements." The development comes after Transportation Minister Miri Regev decided this week that FlyDubai flights to Israel can resume pending clearance from Shin Bet, Mossad and Israel's National Security Council, the outlet reported. A FlyDubai spokesperson told Reuters that the flights will begin again on Dec. 3. FlyDubai flights to Israel have been suspended since FlyDubai Flight FZ1073 on Sept. 30, when a co-pilot allegedly attacked his captain. items.summary_original: Egyptian authorities said Thursday that a driver suspected of causing a fuel tanker crash in Cairo — sparking a massive inferno described by a witness as "God’s hellfire" and leaving 31 dead — has been taken into custody. The deadly blaze erupted Wednesday during rush hour on a major highway surrounding the Egyptian capital, burning 27 vehicles and also leaving 26 injured. As of Thursday, traffic on the Ring Road returned to normal after most of the wreckage was cleared. "It was God’s hellfire on the Ring Road," Salah Ahmed, a microbus driver who witnessed the inferno, told The Associated Press. "People are still in shock." Another witness said to Reuters that victims were found trapped in their vehicles as "they did not have time to get out." STATE DEPARTMENT PRESSES EGYPT TO RESPECT RELIGIOUS FREEDOM AS CHRISTIAN CONVERT FACES POSSIBLE EXECUTION Video footage taken near the scene showed a blaze completely engulfing the highway as people gathered to look at the flames. Egyptian prosecutors said in a statement that authorities had detained the driver of a vehicle suspected of causing the fuel tanker to overturn, which resulted in the fire. They said the driver told investigators he was speeding between lanes when he hit the oil tanker in the rear right. He then lost control of his car and veered far to the right while one of the fuel truck’s tires burst. That caused the fuel tanker to hit the concrete wall of the highway and overturn, leading to the spill of fuel and the fire

items.summary_original: Norwegian airline Norse Atlantic suspended all flights Thursday as its board warned the company may imminently file for bankruptcy if it can't secure short-term financing. "If a short-term financing solution is not secured urgently, it is the Board's intention to file for bankruptcy," the company said in a statement . The airline, which provides long-haul flights between the U.S. and Europe, said it had been discussing with investors a possible takeover that "would include a financing solution." SHIPPING GIANT WARNS STRAIT OF HORMUZ CHAOS IS 'NEW NORMAL' AS TEHRAN SHIFTS 4M BARRELS But, the company added, "There can be no assurance that a viable solution will be found." Pakistan International Airlines (PIA), which contracts jets from Norse through a wet-lease program, shifted all United Kingdom flights to its own Boeing 777 planes, claiming Norse announced the suspension with no notice as PIA passengers were preparing to board. Norse, amid rising fuel costs from the Iran war , began leasing out its Boeing 787 fleet to other airlines as it struggled to make a profit on trans-Atlantic flights. In July, IndiGo, India's largest carrier, announced it would conclude its own wet-lease program with Norse by the end of October. Norse's stock price plummeted and closed down 85%. Most of its value has been wiped out since the start of the year and the stock is now trading at $0.010. items.summary_original: President Donald Trump and NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte are calling on Russia to avoid making any moves "that intentionally, or unintentionally, expand the war" against Ukraine. The declaration came after the pair got together at Trump's Mar-a-Lago residence in Florida on Thanksgiving Eve for what was described as an "outstanding meeting." However, Russia hit Kyiv with ballistic missiles overnight, according to the mayor of the Ukrainian capital. "The meeting was very impactful, with the war between Russia and Ukraine and the conflict in Iran being the primary subjects, as well as all of the record setting achievements that we have made together at the summits in the Hague and at Ankara," Trump and Rutte said in a joint statement. "We also discussed the importance of Russia avoiding any actions that intentionally, or unintentionally, expand the war, and the importance of obtaining a peaceful resolution to the war as rapidly as possible," the statement added. "Lastly, we talked about the importance of continuing to expand defense spending and investment in our industrial base, both in the United States and across NATO." items.summary_original: In keeping with tradition, President Donald Trump marked his sixth Thanksgiving in the executive office with the White House’s annual Turkey Pardon ceremony on Tuesday. His plans for Thanksgiving Day this year remain unannounced — but previous holidays offer a preview of how the president likes to spend the day honoring those who can't be at home for the uniquely American holiday due to service to the country. Last year, Trump spent Thanksgiving at Mar-a-Lago participating in his favorite pastime — golf. But he also used the time in what is known as the "Winter White House" to call Maj. Gen. Dave Gardner, commander of the 101st Airborne Division and Joint Task Force–Southern Border, by video conference and talk with troops deployed along the southern border. TRUMP AND DANA WHITE HONOR MARINE CORPS BAND WITH SIX-FIGURE CHECKS IN FIRST EVENT ON NEW HELIPAD First lady Melania Trump spent the days ahead of the holiday in 2025 visiting Camp Lejeune and Marine Corps Air Station New River with second lady Usha Vance on Nov. 19. They met with military families and made Thanksgiving crafts with children. In 2020, during the final Thanksgiving of his first term, Trump remained at the White House and made calls to six deployed military units representing every branch of the armed forces, including troops in Kuwait and sailors aboard the USS Winston Churchill in the Red Sea. items.summary_original: Donald Trump carried Mississippi by nearly 23 points in 2024. Two years later, Democrat Scott Colom won the state’s Senate race, ending a Republican hold that had lasted more than four decades. Colom’s victory was part of a string of Democratic breakthroughs during the midterms in places Trump had carried by double digits. Democrats also won Senate races in Kansas and South Carolina, captured the Texas governor’s office and flipped a Republican-held House seat deep in Trump country in Indiana that had not elected a Democrat since 1990. The results stand out for more than the presidential margins as well — Democrats broke Senate streaks that had lasted decades and defeated Republican incumbents in races many expected the GOP to hold, including one where the Democratic challenger spent next to nothing on television advertisements. FOX NEWS VOTER POLL: HOW DEMOCRATS TOOK CONTROL OF THE SENATE Here are five of the year’s most striking upsets: Trump carried the state by nearly 23 points in 2024, and a Democrat had not won a U.S. Senate race in Mississippi since 1982. Several major election forecasters rated the contest Solid Republican for much of the cycle, before shifting it to Likely Republican as the race tightened. Colom, a district attorney, defeated Republican incumbent Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith, R-Miss., by less than one percentage point, 49.36% to 48.54%, according to Associated Press election results. items.summary_original: The turkey may be a holiday bargain, but rising prices for meat, dairy and fresh foods could make the rest of the Thanksgiving spread cost much more this year. Richard Volpe, a professor of agribusiness at Cal Poly San Luis Obispo, told Fox News Digital that sustained high energy costs in the midst of the Iran war — particularly for diesel — are pushing up grocery prices just as households prepare to host holiday meals. Surging prices of ham and eggnog, in particular, could put a damper on some holiday favorites. "Most of the biggest increases are things like fruits, vegetables and meats," Volpe said. "Fresh and refrigerated foods feel those costs sooner than shelf-stable products." 7 COSTCO THANKSGIVING FOOD DEALS AND STEALS THAT SHOPPERS CAN'T MISS THIS HOLIDAY SEASON Dairy is also especially energy and transportation intensive, putting holiday staples such as butter and eggnog under pressure. Volpe said shoppers willing to switch brands and take advantage of store promotions can keep holiday meals more affordable . "If you are less worried about brand or banner loyalty, and you’re able to follow promotions and look for these sort of aggressive, enticing deals, there are still ways to achieve savings and to keep those Thanksgiving and holiday dinners relatively affordable," Volpe said. items.summary_original: Illinois Gov. JB Pritzker , a Democrat, is being accused of putting partisan politics over kids' educational needs after he decided to opt out of the Federal Scholarship Tax Credit program, prompting criticism from parents and education advocacy groups. Pritzker announced on Tuesday that his state will not opt into the program, which was signed into law by President Donald Trump last year as part of the One Big Beautiful Bill Act. The governor described the program as a school voucher, while advocacy groups argued that he mischaracterized the plan. "At a time when public school education needs investments more than ever, we should not siphon money from public schools for private education – especially as the Trump Administration's policies decimate education," Pritzker said in a statement. "We have a responsibility to do right by all of our students. Taxpayer funding should not subsidize donations to private schools that could discriminate based on religion, sexual orientation, or other characteristics." The program allows people to receive federal tax credits for donations up to $1,700 to authorized scholarship-granting organizations (SGOs), which distribute the donated scholarship funds to eligible families to be used on private or public educational expenses, including private school tuition, tutoring services, textbooks and more. items.summary_original: The decade-long legal battle against Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu suffered a major blow Wednesday after judges cast doubt on key corruption charges, prompting the Israeli leader to declare that his trial had "fallen apart" and demand an immediate end to the proceedings. A three-judge panel at the Jerusalem District Court suggested that Attorney General Gali Baharav-Miara consider dropping the most serious case against Netanyahu, questioned whether a criminal offense occurred in a second case and recommended resolving a third through a plea deal. "Today, the trial fell apart," Netanyahu said in an evening address following the proceedings, according to The Times of Israel . FROM INTELLIGENCE SHARING TO MISSILE DEFENSE, HOW ISRAEL'S PARTNERSHIP PROTECTS AMERICAN SECURITY "Ten years ago, I said, ‘There will be nothing because there was nothing.’ But it took 10 years for this truth to be revealed to everyone," he said. "Citizens of Israel, this trial must end immediately. And what also needs to end immediately is what came out of it — the hatred, the incitement, the division." The court's intervention dealt a major setback to prosecutors more than six years after Netanyahu's trial began and roughly a decade after authorities launched the initial probe into him. Judges had summoned Baharav-Miara to court Wednesday amid concerns over the strength of the prosecution's evidence and whether continuing the cases served the public interest. items.summary_original: A federal appeals court handed President Donald Trump a legal victory Monday, reviving his bid to wrest his New York hush money case from state court and potentially overturn his felony conviction on presidential immunity grounds. The 2nd U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals ruled that an August decision by the late U. S. District Judge Alvin Hellerstein, a Clinton appointee who died in October, that denied Trump's second transfer bid was improper. The criminal case centered on Trump's reimbursement of his then-attorney Michael Cohen, who paid adult film actress Stormy Daniels $130,000 shortly before the 2016 election to keep her from publicizing an alleged sexual encounter with Trump a decade earlier. Trump, who denies the encounter, was found guilty in May 2024 of 34 felony counts of falsifying business records. items.summary_original: Far-left lawmakers are facing accusations of hypocrisy for criticizing corporate influence in politics while accepting campaign contributions from influential executives in industries including defense and healthcare. A new investigation looking into Federal Election Commission filings found socialist-aligned candidates who pledged to reject corporate PAC contributions still took the cash from PAC's and corporate executives. "If you're taking money from them, at least be man enough to admit you're going to take the money," Rep.-elect Jerry Carl, R-Ala., told Fox News Digital in reference to Rep. Rashida Tlaib, D-Mich. Filings first flagged by anti-DEI nonprofit 1792 Exchange were reviewed by Fox News Digital. They show Tlaib accepted checks in 2023 and 2025 totaling $10,600 from L3Harris executive defense contractor Faisal Munir, even after she authored an op-ed in 2025 criticizing lawmakers who financially benefit from the defense industry. Yet all three took cash from PACs and corporate executives, as noted in the investigation. items.summary_original: A DC federal judge, previously dubbed by President Donald Trump as an "anti- Trump Hater," blocked Trump's second attempt to restrict birthright citizenship in a Wednesday ruling. U.S. District Judge Christopher Cooper , who was recently in Trump's crosshairs after ruling against efforts to shut down the Kennedy Center for renovations and add Trump's name to the cultural institution, issued a 67-page ruling striking down an August executive order that barred U.S. -born children whose parents are suspected terrorists or gang members, or children born through surrogacy to foreign parents, from citizenship eligibility. Cooper's ruling comes months after the Supreme Court struck down Trump's initial executive order, signed on his first day back in office. The order attempted to deny birthright citizenship to U.S.-born children whose mothers were in the country illegally or temporarily and whose fathers were neither U.S. citizens nor green card holders. items.summary_original: House Republicans are optimistic that President Donald Trump could sign a bipartisan immigration reform bill before Democrats take control of Congress. They warn that if the president waits until January it could result in legislation containing more "extreme" language that opens the door for amnesty. "Yes, it's going to happen under this Congress," Rep. Don Bacon, R-Neb., told Fox News Digital, pointing to the country's labor shortages and Republicans' declining support among Hispanic voters as reasons to pursue immigration reform. "I think it's a win-win for a country, we get a much-needed workforce while providing some accountability for misbehavior." Bacon's remarks come after Trump signaled during a recent "60 Minutes" interview that he would be open to immigration reform, potentially creating an opportunity for lawmakers to advance the Dignity Act, a bill introduced by Rep. Maria Elvira Salazar, R-Fla., in 2025. The findings, published Monday by independent Russian news outlets Meduza and Mediazona , are based on leaked Russian government records and statistical analysis. "The only entity that can officially disclose casualty figures is the Russian Defense Ministry," Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told reporters Wednesday, according to The Moscow Times. PUTIN'S WAR MACHINE TIED TO TROUBLING RECRUITMENT OF YOUNG WOMEN AS NEW DEALS EMERGE Peskov urged reporters to disregard other figures but offered no updated official death toll. The investigation draws on records obtained by the hacking groups Belarusian Cyber Partisans and Silent Crow after they breached Russia's federal statistics agency, Rosstat. Researchers identified at least 490,000 registered military deaths by late September 2026. However, delays in registering fatalities and soldiers who remain officially listed as missing but are believed to be dead led researchers to estimate that the actual toll had likely reached 700,000 or more by that time. items.summary_original: Attorney General Todd Blanche is mobilizing civil litigators across the Justice Department in an all-hands-on-deck push to fight tens of thousands of legal filings by detained migrants asking federal courts to review whether their imprisonment is lawful. Blanche issued a three-page memo Tuesday calling on attorneys working outside of immigration issues to assist in the lawsuits described by Blanche as "frivolous" and an attempt to "thwart President Trump's promise to the American people to prioritize their safety and security." The pre-Thanksgiving memo comes as the Justice Department has been hit with 97, 000 habeas corpus petition filings since January 2025, including close to 10,000 new petitions filed since October. Typically, the Justice Department faces only a few hundred habeas corpus cases a year. As President Donald Trump has made mass deportations a centerpiece of his second administration, with Department of Homeland Security figures showing nearly 1.2 million illegal immigrants removed to date, the Justice Department has seen a wave of petitions. items.summary_original: Before polling began to show dire warning signs for the GOP ahead of the midterm elections , some in conservative circles felt they had a not-so-secret weapon that would give them an edge over their Democratic rivals — a massive amount of cash. Across the Republican National Committee, Senate Leadership Fund, Congressional Leadership Fund, National Republican Congressional Committee and the National Republican Senatorial Committee, the GOP brought in roughly $1.7 billion in funds to fuel its ill-fated midterm campaigns. The five equivalent Democratic committees, meanwhile, raised well over $300 million less than that total but walked away with massive pickups in even traditionally deep red strongholds like Texas, South Carolina, Kansas and Mississippi. Experts from across the political spectrum explained this result to Fox News Digital by arguing that the impact of money on politics is less than what many in the public may assume and that massive fundraising hauls can only take a party so far when it faces political headwinds as strong as those weathered by the GOP in the run-up to election night. Their research documented 2,465 anti-Christian hate crimes and incidents in 2025, with France , England and Wales, Germany and Austria recording the highest totals. "Our primary concern with the new data is that anti-Christian attacks that target persons, individuals themselves, have risen," OIDAC executive director Anja Tang told Fox News Digital. "Clergy and people responsible for places of worship were those who were most attacked and also where numbers increased most strongly." CHRISTIAN WOMAN PLEADS NOT GUILTY TO NEW 'ORWELLIAN' CHARGES FOR STANDING AND SILENT PRAYER She added, "These would be people who were present, were visible, recognizable as Christians and kind of associated with a church." Tang noted that while OIDAC’s numbers are "quite conservative," saying "aggression against individuals is highly underreported" across Europe. The group said French authorities recorded a 70% increase in attacks on individuals, the highest in Europe, although Tang notes the French government has not yet published a detailed explanation of the increase. items.summary_original: The Trump administration has renewed internal discussions about potentially targeting senior Iranian regime leaders in strikes that some officials believe could end the ongoing war, according to reports. Citing a U. S. official and another source, NBC News reported Tuesday that some officials believe eliminating senior figures could pressure Tehran to end the conflict by showing that Washington can locate and strike the regime's leadership at any time. Though the option has long been under consideration, it has "been under renewed discussion in recent weeks" as President Donald Trump deliberates over the next phase of the war, two sources told the outlet. The deliberations come amid reports that Iran could be developing a radioactive "dirty bomb" and a report citing U. S. intelligence assessments of potential Iranian plots involving chemical weapons aimed at senior officials in Washington. TRUMP WARNS IRAN ABOUT REPORTED PLOT AGAINST ADMIN OFFICIALS: 'WE TAKE IT VERY SERIOUSLY' "We know a lot about what's happening in Iran. We know everything they say. We know who they are, where they are. We'll find out about it. We will not allow that," Trump had told reporters at the White House Nov. 20. Milad Armoun, 27, and Navid Najaran, 34, are scheduled to be executed in the early hours of Wednesday, Nov. 25, according to Iran Human Rights (IHRNGO). The men were transferred to solitary confinement on Nov. 21 after Iran's Supreme Court upheld their death sentences . items.summary_original: Excerpts from the late Pope Francis ' private diary published Tuesday reveal that the pontiff endured a two-year spiritual crisis beginning in 2021, writing that he felt tempted by the devil and struggled with the weight of wielding power over the Catholic Church. The 160-page volume, "The Private Diary of Pope Francis," was compiled by Cardinal Victor Fernandez and spans entries from December 1992 through August 2024 — eight months before Francis died in April 2025 at age 88 — marking the first papal diary made public since the 1960s. In a December 2022 entry, Francis described his crisis as "all mixed with governance issues, pressure regarding decisions to make, and aridity and desolation," adding that he resisted becoming a leader "who uses others like puppets." MYSTERIOUS BLOOD-SOAKED RELIC LINKED TO HISTORY'S MOST BELOVED SAINT, ST. FRANCIS OF ASSISI, GOES ON DISPLAY Across the entries, Francis wrote that he believed he had seen the devil three times — including during a Vatican meeting — and recalled a June 2018 vision of hell . "Last night I saw the entrance to Hell," he wrote in the 2018 entry. "I peeked in to look a little, and it terrified me. I grabbed the Rosary as a weapon. I thank the Lord for this help." Reacting Tuesday on "Varney Co.," Fox News contributor and theologian Jonathan Morris said he was most struck not by the late pope's spiritual struggles , but by the Vatican's decision to publish them. items.summary_original: Israel accused Iran of developing chemical weapons Tuesday and raised the possibility of a preemptive strike to prevent Tehran from using them, warning that the regime seeks a strategic advantage after major setbacks in its war with Israel and the United States. Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz told reporters in Tel Aviv that Israel and the U.S. have intelligence indicating Iran began developing chemical weapons after their joint military campaign launched Feb. 28. Katz declined to disclose how far the program has progressed or where the weapons are being developed, though he noted Israeli intelligence has monitored Iran's effort for months and said that operational plans are in place. BLINKEN WARNS US GROUND INVASION OF IRAN WOULD BE 'ABSOLUTE DISASTER' AS TEHRAN ESCALATES ATTACKS "Iran is in the process of developing chemical weapons," Katz said, according to Israel's i24NEWS . "This intelligence information reached both the United States and Israel," he said. "Israel is determined not to allow Iran to acquire this kind of chemical weapons capability that would threaten the country and the entire region," he added. Latvian President Edgars Rinkēvičs said Western leaders may be underestimating the threat posed by Russian President Vladimir Putin because they fail to fully understand the ideological and historical beliefs driving the Kremlin’s foreign policy. "The appetite for the risk is growing in Russia," Rinkēvičs said. "We see numbers of arson attacks. Some assassination plots. Acts of sabotage." "We see that the number of attacks is rising, but we still see that, at this point, it may change very quickly. It may change maybe in weeks or months or a couple of months' time," he said. The Latvian leader pointed to recent cooperation between Latvian and Estonian intelligence services that he said resulted in arrests in Estonia and prevented an attack against a defense factory. items.summary_original: Iranian authorities subjected a female singer and four members of her concert team to 74 lashes each Monday after she defied the Islamic Republic’s restrictions on women by performing without a hijab in a viral YouTube concert, their lawyers said. Parastoo Ahmadi, 29, and her four male co-defendants were flogged in the Iranian city of Qom, defense attorney Mostafa Nili told Iranian news outlet Emtedad, according to Reuters. The five were also banned from traveling abroad and engaging in artistic and musical activities for two years. IRAN'S REGIME CAME FOR TEENAGE TWINS. THEIR FATE OFFERS A GLIMPSE OF TEHRAN'S WIDENING DEATH CAMPAIGN One of the defendants’ lawyers told the BBC Monday that efforts to overturn the ruling, reduce the punishment or suspend its enforcement had failed. Defense attorneys also sought to postpone the flogging, but authorities insisted on carrying out the sentence immediately. The punishment sparked outrage among Iranian artists and human rights advocates , who condemned the regime’s restrictions on women and artistic expression. Bahar Ghandehari, director of advocacy at the U.S.-based Center for Human Rights in Iran (CHRI), told the BBC that Ahmadi’s flogging was "a flagrant violation of her fundamental rights" and demonstrated the authorities’ determination to suppress women’s freedoms and punish those who challenge discriminatory laws. items.summary_original: The Ukrainian sea drone strike that capsized and sank a Russian warship in Libya on Sunday risks a "serious escalation" of the nearly five-year war, a former U.S. national security adviser warned Monday, calling the operation a "giant tantrum" by Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy. Morgan Murphy , a former press secretary to the secretary of defense, also told Fox News Digital that the nighttime attack on the Russian corvette Mercury in the Libyan port city of Benghazi could further strain relations between Zelenskyy and President Donald Trump, while echoing frustrations that he said also plagued former President Joe Biden's administration. "The strike on the Russian corvette Mercury in North Africa — in Libya specifically — is a serious escalation of the war in Ukraine," Murphy claimed. "Calling the Benghazi strike a giant tantrum could be one interpretation of it, and it's not unusual behavior for him," Murphy said of Zelenskyy. items.summary_original: NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte warned Monday that creating a separate European army could undermine the alliance’s ability to respond quickly to a Russian attack, as Moscow continues to ramp up its military capabilities during the ongoing war in Ukraine. Speaking at the 72nd annual session of the NATO Parliamentary Assembly in Berlin , Rutte cautioned that competing military command structures could hold up decisions in a crisis, warning that Russia’s "war machine" is running at full throttle and could also pose a threat to Europe long after the war ends. "What I would counsel against is having all the nations with their own militaries working together in NATO and then on top of that having a big European structure, because then if Putin attacks, we will first need two or three weeks to agree who will do what, and then he will probably end up in Rotterdam before we have decided. So that has been my argument," Rutte said, according to Ukrainska Pravda . NATO JETS SHOOT DOWN DRONE IN LITHUANIAN AIRSPACE AS RUSSIA GROWS 'INCREASINGLY RECKLESS,' RUTTE SAYS Rutte pointed to the United States as a model for an integrated military, arguing that European countries would also need to move beyond separate national forces to establish a unified army. "My point has always been that if you have a European military, you cannot also have national militaries. The United States has one military."
